get.description: The public keys that verify vendor-api tokens. Public keys only, never private ones.
Liveness: the process is up. Does not touch any dependency.
Readiness: every dependency answers. 503 if any check fails or times out.

The admin behind the token: the id and the roles in it. Nothing is looked up, because
admins live in identity-api; this is the first admin endpoint and a check for Phase 3.

post.description: Sets a new password, ends every session of the user and starts a new one.

Sends a reset link only if the address belongs to an active user; the answer never says
which. Limited per IP and per address (as typed), so it cannot be used to flood an inbox.

`401 invalid_credentials` for an unknown email, a wrong password, a user who has no
password yet, a disabled user and an unverified email alike (a separate answer for unverified
would reveal, after a signup, whether an address was already registered). A rejected or
suspended vendor is `403 vendor_not_allowed`.
Sends a new link only if the user exists and is unverified; the answer never says which.

Accepts an invite or a reset link with a new password.

It activates an invited user, marks the email verified (the link proved it), spends the
token and ends every session of the user. A token that is unknown, used or expired is one
generic `400 invalid_token`. It does not sign the user in: they log in with the new password.

Creates a pending vendor and its owner, and emails a verification link.

A registered email gets the same answer, and an "you already have an account" email.
Spends a verification token. An unknown, used or expired one is one generic 400.

get.description: The signed-in vendor user, their role and their vendor. No password hash, no tokens.
The vendor's products, most recently changed first.

post.description:
A new `draft` product. Images and variants can be added later, but are needed to submit.
`409 sku_taken` if the vendor already uses the SKU (case is ignored, archived products keep
theirs).

delete.description:
Deletes a product that was never submitted; archives one that was (it keeps its history
and SKU, and an approved one goes off sale). `409 product_in_review` while in review.

put.description:
Replaces the content of the revision being edited. Editing an approved product leaves
what is live untouched: it creates a new pending revision (`working`) that goes live only
when approved. `409 product_in_review` while a version is in review. The SKU cannot change.

post.description:
Sends the revision being edited for review. It needs at least one active variant and one
image (`422 product_incomplete`). The submitted revision is frozen.

schema.title: Response List Users V1 Vendor Users Get

post.description:
Invites a staff member by email: an `invited` user with no password and an emailed link.

An address that is already used anywhere (any vendor) gets the same answer and no email, so
the endpoint cannot be used to find out who is registered.

patch.description:
Disables or enables a staff user. Disabling ends their sessions at once. The owner cannot
be disabled (so nobody can disable themselves), and another vendor's user is a 404.

post.description: A new invite for a user who has not set a password yet; it ends the older ones.
